answer.text:
No — bakery is not inside the fresh workstream now. It was removed from the fresh Phase 2 scope at the 17 November 2025 go/no-go and set up as its own separate workstream, which started in March 2026. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5]

March 2024 – June 2025: bakery was inside fresh. At the July 2024 implementation kickoff, Lena Fischer listed the fresh scope as "Produce, dairy, bakery, the chilled ready meals" [T05U0116], and Marco Rossi's June 2025 sequencing proposal treated bakery as the third of three fresh waves [E03M008]. [6] [7]

August–October 2025: bakery still in fresh, but failing. UAT ran on all four fresh categories, and the weekly updates flagged "Bakery accuracy poor. Likely a scope change rather than a defect" [R01M009], with the October steering report expecting to recommend descoping it [R02M004]. [8] [9]

17 November 2025: bakery removed from fresh. At the go/no-go, Sofia Almeida explained bakery was poor because roughly half is baked in store and "is not really an ordering problem" [T17U0032][T17U0033], and Lena Fischer decided: "Go live on produce, dairy and chilled ready meals. Bakery comes later as its own thing" [T17U0047][T17U0049]. The weekly update recorded "Bakery descoped" [R01M007], and the November steering report states "Bakery descoped to a separate workstream starting March 2026" [R02M003]. [10] [11] [1] [2] [3] [4]

2026: bakery runs as its own workstream. Scoping with Meridian began in January [R02M002], the workstream started in March [R01M002], and the design workshop in March 2026 treats it as a separate build where Meridian owns the production plan and RELEX owns the demand signal [T20U0003]. [12] [5] [13]

So the current answer: bakery is a separate workstream outside fresh, with its own scope, partner (Meridian) and timeline. [4] [12] [13]

citations.quote:
Hello both,

Following our conversation, a proposal for how we sequence Phase 2.

Rather than delivering all four fresh categories together in one go-live, we would
deliver produce and dairy first, then chilled ready meals, then bakery. Three smaller
go-lives roughly six weeks apart.

The advantage is that value starts landing earlier and each wave de-risks the next. The
disadvantage is more cutover events and a longer total elapsed time, which I know is in
tension with the twelve-month window.

If this works for you we would build the plan around it. Happy to discuss.

Marco Rossi
